groups.title: Abortion
notes: Compromise in the middle, inside the right: sanctity-of-life vs late-term horror / no theocracy. Not the left/right abortion triple in hidden-majority-patterns.md.

statements.text: Abortion ends a child's life. I don't think of it as ordinary healthcare, and I want far fewer of them.
Late-term abortion is horrific. Early pregnancy is more complicated, and I don't want the state enforcing a church teaching on people who don't believe it.

Abortion ends a child's life, and I'd prefer far fewer abortions. I still don't want the law to leave a woman no time to decide. I'd be okay with it if abortion were allowed during the first 12-16 weeks and forbidden after that except in serious medical situations. This isn't my ideal outcome, but I'd rather get this settled than keep fighting over it forever.

groups.title: Markets and provision for the poor
notes: Different reasons, same conclusion. Commonality is the conclusion with neither stewardship nor Hayek attached.

statements.text: Caring for the poor is the church's work. A large welfare state often crowds that out and treats people as clients instead of neighbors.
Free markets create prosperity. A large welfare state traps people in dependence and costs more than it delivers.

I come to this because I think caring for the poor is the church's work, not because I think the market is an idol. I want ordinary people to be able to earn a living and keep more of what they earn. I do not want a larger welfare state as the default way of providing for people; private charity and local help should do more of that work. The remaining safety-net details can be argued separately, in good faith.

groups.title: LGBT unbundling
notes: Atomize adult gay neighbors from rushing minors into medical transition. Reaffirm so signing is not betrayal. Commonality does not require Christians to affirm same-sex marriage or secular signers to affirm a theology of sex.

statements.text: Marriage, as I understand it from Scripture, is a man and a woman. I still don't want to treat gay people as enemies.
Gay adults should be able to marry. Schools treating gender-distressed kids as a medical-transition pipeline is a different issue, and I don't want that.

I still believe marriage, in the Christian sense, is a man and a woman. Gay adults should be treated as neighbors, not enemies. Whatever the civil law does about adult relationships, I do not want schools or clinics to rush minors into medical transition.
